title.en: Volume 177 Biographies 64: Zhang Siming, Wu Yuangui, Zhang Sheng, Zang Mengjie, Chen Hao
title.raw: 卷一百七十七 列傳第六十四: 張思明 吳元珪 張昇 臧夢解 陳顥 Volume 177 Biographies 64: Zhang Siming, Wu Yuangui, Zhang Sheng, Zang Mengjie, Chen Hao

sentences.zh: 張思明

translations.literal: Zhang Siming
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Siming

sentences.zh: 張思明，字士瞻，其先獲嘉人，後​​徙居輝州。

translations.literal: Zhang Siming, styled Shizhan, was originally from Huojia; his family later moved to Huizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Siming, whose style name was Shizhan, came from Huojia by ancestry but later settled in Huizhou.

sentences.zh: 思明穎悟過人，讀書日記千言。

translations.literal: Siming was exceptionally quick-witted; in reading he could memorize a thousand characters per day.
translations.idiomatic: Siming was unusually quick of mind and could commit a thousand characters to memory in a single day of study.

sentences.zh: 至元十九年，由侍儀司舍人辟御史臺掾，又辟尚書省掾。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year of Zhiyuan, through his post as attendant of the Ceremonial Office he was recruited as a secretary of the Censorate, and again as a secretary of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year of the Zhiyuan reign, on the strength of his post as ceremonial attendant he was recruited first as a Censorate clerk and then as a Secretariat clerk.

sentences.zh: 左丞相阿合馬既死，世祖追咎其奸欺，命尚書簿問遺孽。

translations.literal: After the Left Chancellor Ahmad died, Kublai pursued blame for his treachery and deceit and ordered the Secretariat to interrogate his surviving accomplices.
translations.idiomatic: After Left Chancellor Ahmad died, Kublai held him accountable for treachery and fraud and ordered the Secretariat to investigate his remaining associates.

sentences.zh: 一日，召右丞何榮祖、左丞馬紹，盡輸其贓以入，思明抱牘從，日已昏，命讀之，自昏達曙，帝聽忘疲，曰：「讀人吐音，大似侍儀舍人。

translations.literal: One day he summoned Right Chancellor He Rongzu and Left Chancellor Ma Shao to present in full all the bribes involved; Siming followed carrying the documents. The day had already grown dark when the Emperor ordered them read aloud—from dusk until dawn. The Emperor listened without tiring and said, "The reader's enunciation sounds very much like a ceremonial attendant."
translations.idiomatic: One day he summoned Right Chancellor He Rongzu and Left Chancellor Ma Shao to submit a full account of the bribes, with Siming following behind carrying the dossiers. By the time the Emperor ordered them read aloud, night had fallen; he listened from dusk until dawn without tiring and remarked, "The reader's delivery sounds very much like a ceremonial attendant."

sentences.zh: 」右丞對曰：「正由舍人選為掾。

translations.literal: " The Right Chancellor replied, "It is because he was chosen from among the attendants for this secretary post."
translations.idiomatic: " The Right Chancellor answered, "He was promoted to clerk from among the ceremonial attendants."

sentences.zh: 」帝奇之，曰：「斯人可用。

translations.literal: " The Emperor was impressed and said, "This man can be used."
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor was struck by this and said, "This man is fit for service."

sentences.zh: 」明日，擢為大都路治中。

translations.literal: " The next day he was promoted to assistant administrator of the Dadu Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: " The following day Siming was promoted to assistant administrator of the Dadu Circuit.

sentences.zh: 思明以超遷逾等，固辭，乃改湖廣行省都事。

translations.literal: Siming, considering the leap in rank beyond proper grade, firmly declined; he was then changed to director of the Huguang Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Siming regarded the promotion as a leap beyond his proper rank and firmly declined, whereupon he was appointed director of the Huguang Branch Secretariat instead.

sentences.zh: 元貞元年，召為中書省檢校，六曹無滯案，遷戶部主事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanzhen he was summoned as inspector of the Secretariat; in the six bureaus there were no backlog cases, and he was transferred to registrar of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yuanzhen he was called to serve as Secretariat inspector; under him the six bureaus cleared their backlogs, and he was promoted to registrar in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 大德初，擢左司都事，有獻西域秤法，思明以惑眾不用。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Dade era he was promoted to director of the Left Secretariat; someone presented a Western Regions method of weighing, but Siming refused to adopt it on the grounds that it would mislead the people.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Dade reign he rose to director of the Left Secretariat. When someone offered a Western Regions system of weights, Siming rejected it as likely to confuse the public.

sentences.zh: 初立海道運糧萬戶府於江浙，受除者憚涉險，不行，思明請升等以優之，因著為令。

translations.literal: When the Maritime Grain Transport Ten-thousand-household Office was first established in Jiang-Zhe, appointees feared the perils of the route and refused to take up their posts; Siming requested that their rank be raised as an incentive, and this was written into regulation.
translations.idiomatic: When the Maritime Grain Transport Ten-thousand-household Office was first set up in Jiang-Zhe, appointees shrank from the dangers of the sea route and declined to serve. Siming asked that their rank be raised as an inducement, and the measure was codified as law.

sentences.zh: 五年，轉吏部郎中。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was transferred to director in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was transferred to director in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 九年，改集賢司直。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was changed to direct secretary of the Hall of Gathered Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was reassigned as direct secretary of the Hall of Gathered Worthies.

sentences.zh: 十年，除江浙行中書省左右司郎中。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was appointed director of the Left and Right Secretariats of the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was appointed director of the Left and Right Secretariats in the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 十一年春，兩浙大饑，首贊發廩賑之。

translations.literal: In the spring of the eleventh year a great famine struck the two Zhe circuits; he was the first to urge opening the granaries for relief.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the eleventh year both Zhe circuits suffered severe famine; he was foremost in urging that public granaries be opened for relief.

sentences.zh: 至大三年，遷兩浙鹽運使，未上，入參議樞密院事，改中書省左司郎中。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhida he was transferred to salt transport commissioner of the two Zhe circuits but did not take up the post; he entered service as deliberator of the Bureau of Military Affairs and was changed to director of the Left Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhida he was named salt transport commissioner for the two Zhe circuits but never assumed the post; instead he became deliberator of the Bureau of Military Affairs and was reassigned as director of the Left Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 皇慶元年，再授兩浙鹽運使，歲課羨贏，僚屬請上增數，思明曰：「贏縮不常，萬一以增為額，是我希一己之榮，遺百世之害。

translations.literal: In the first year of Huangqing he was again appointed salt transport commissioner of the two Zhe circuits. When the year's levy showed a surplus, his subordinates asked to report an increased quota. Siming said, "Surplus and shortfall are not constant; if by chance the increase were made the fixed quota, I would be seeking personal glory at the cost of harm lasting a hundred generations."
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Huangqing he was again appointed salt transport commissioner for the two Zhe circuits. When the year's receipts ran above quota, his staff urged reporting a higher target. Siming said, "Surpluses and shortfalls do not hold steady; if we fixed the quota at this year's gain, I would be trading one man's honor for a hundred generations of harm."

sentences.zh: 」二年，召為戶部尚書。

translations.literal: " In the second year he was summoned as Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: " In the second year he was summoned to serve as Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 延祐元年，進參議中書省事；

translations.literal: In the first year of Yanyou he was advanced to deliberator of Secretariat affairs;
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yanyou he was promoted to deliberator of Secretariat affairs;

sentences.zh: 三年，拜中書參知政事。

translations.literal: in the third year he was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: and in the third year he was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 仁宗即位，浮屠妙總統有寵，敕中書官其弟五品，思明執不可。

translations.literal: When Renzong took the throne, the Buddhist monk Miaozong was in favor, and an edict ordered the Secretariat to grant his younger brother a fifth-rank office; Siming held firm that this could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: When Renzong came to the throne, the Buddhist monk Miaozong enjoyed imperial favor, and an edict directed the Secretariat to give his younger brother a fifth-rank post. Siming refused to comply.

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，召見切責之，對曰：「選法，天下公器。

translations.literal: The Emperor was greatly angered, summoned him, and sharply rebuked him. He replied, "The selection law is a public instrument of the realm."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor flew into a rage, summoned him, and rebuked him sharply. Siming answered, "The law of appointment is a public trust of the realm."

sentences.zh: 徑路一開，來者雜遝。

translations.literal: Once a shortcut is opened, those who come will crowd in disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Once a back door is opened, petitioners will pour in without end.

sentences.zh: 故寧違旨獲戾，不忍隳祖宗成憲，使四方得窺陛下淺深也。

translations.literal: Therefore I would rather disobey the edict and incur blame than destroy the established statutes of the ancestors and let the four quarters glimpse the depth or shallowness of Your Majesty's resolve.
translations.idiomatic: I would rather defy the edict and bear punishment than tear down the statutes our ancestors fixed and let the realm gauge how deep or shallow Your Majesty's standards run.

sentences.zh: 」帝心然其言，而業已許之，曰：「卿可姑與之，後勿為例。

translations.literal: " The Emperor inwardly approved his words, but having already promised the appointment, said, "You may provisionally grant it, but do not make this a precedent hereafter."
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor was persuaded in his heart, yet having already given his word he said, "Grant it for now, but let this never become a precedent."

sentences.zh: 」乃為萬億庫提舉，不與散官。

translations.literal: " He was then made superintendent of the Wanyi Treasury, without a regular civil rank.
translations.idiomatic: " The brother was made superintendent of the Wanyi Treasury, without a regular civil rank.

sentences.zh: 久之，近臣疾其持法峭直，日構讒間，出為工部尚書。

translations.literal: After a long while, court favorites resented his stern and upright enforcement of law and daily wove slander against him; he was sent out as Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In time court favorites, resenting his rigid uprightness in law, daily spread slander until he was transferred out as Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 帝問左右曰：「張士瞻居工部，得無怏怏乎？

translations.literal: The Emperor asked those around him, "Now that Zhang Shizhan is at the Ministry of Works, is he not discontent?"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor asked his attendants, "With Zhang Shizhan at the Ministry of Works, is he not sulking?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「勤政如初。

translations.literal: " They replied, "He is as diligent in office as before."
translations.idiomatic: " They answered, "He is as diligent as ever."

sentences.zh: 」帝嘉嘆之，命授宣政院副使。

translations.literal: " The Emperor praised and sighed over this and ordered him appointed Vice Commissioner of the Xuanzheng Court.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor expressed admiration and ordered him appointed Vice Commissioner of the Xuanzheng Court.

sentences.zh: 五年，除西京宣慰使。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was appointed pacification commissioner of Xijing.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was appointed pacification commissioner of Xijing.

sentences.zh: 嶺北戍士多貧者，歲凶，相挺為變，思明威惠並行，邊境乃安。

translations.literal: Many garrison soldiers north of the ranges were poor; in a bad year they rose together in mutiny. Siming combined sternness with kindness, and the borderlands were then pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Many frontier garrison troops north of the ranges were destitute; when famine struck they banded together in unrest. Siming combined authority with kindness, and the border was restored to calm.

sentences.zh: 因疏和林運糧不便事十一條，帝勞以端硯、上尊。

translations.literal: He thereupon memorialized eleven points on the inconveniences of grain transport to Karakorum; the Emperor rewarded him with an inkstone of duan stone and fine wine.
translations.idiomatic: He then submitted eleven memorialized points on the hardships of supplying grain to Karakorum, and the Emperor rewarded him with a duan inkstone and imperial wine.

sentences.zh: 會左丞相哈散辭職，帝不允，其請益堅，帝詰之曰：「朕任卿未專邪？

translations.literal: When Left Chancellor Hasan sought to resign, the Emperor would not allow it; as his request grew more insistent, the Emperor questioned him, saying, "Have I not entrusted you with full authority?"
translations.idiomatic: When Left Chancellor Hasan sought to resign, the Emperor refused; as Hasan pressed harder, the Emperor demanded, "Have I not given you my full trust?"

translations.literal: " He said, "No."
translations.idiomatic: " He answered, "No."

sentences.zh: 」曰：「近臣有撓政者邪？

translations.literal: " He said, "Are there favorites interfering with government?"
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor asked, "Are there favorites obstructing your work?"

sentences.zh: 」曰：「無有也。

translations.literal: " He said, "There are none."
translations.idiomatic: " He answered, "None."

sentences.zh: 」「然則何為而辭？

translations.literal: " "Then why resign?"
translations.idiomatic: " "Then why do you insist on resigning?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「臣自揆才薄，恐誤陛下國事，若必欲任臣，願荐一人為助。

translations.literal: " He replied, "I judge my own talent slight and fear I may err in Your Majesty's state affairs; if you must employ me, I wish to recommend one man to assist."
translations.idiomatic: " He replied, "I find my own talents wanting and fear I may harm Your Majesty's governance; if you must keep me in office, I beg to recommend one man to assist me."

sentences.zh: 」帝問：「為誰？

translations.literal: " The Emperor asked, "Who?"
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor asked, "Whom?"

sentences.zh: 朕能從汝。

translations.literal: I can follow your recommendation.
translations.idiomatic: I will do as you say.

sentences.zh: 」哈散再拜謝曰；

translations.literal: " Hasan bowed twice in thanks and said:
translations.idiomatic: " Hasan bowed twice and said:

sentences.zh: 「臣願得張思明。

translations.literal: "I wish to have Zhang Siming."
translations.idiomatic: "I wish to have Zhang Siming."

sentences.zh: 」即日拜思明中書參知政事。

translations.literal: " That same day Siming was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: " That same day Siming was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 比召至，車駕幸上都，見於道，慰勉之曰：「卿向不負朕注委，故朕用哈散言，復起汝。

translations.literal: By the time he was summoned and arrived, the imperial carriage was proceeding to Shangdu; the Emperor met him on the road and comforted him, saying, "You did not fail the trust I placed in you before; therefore I followed Hasan's words and have raised you again."
translations.idiomatic: When he was summoned and arrived, the Emperor was already on the road to Shangdu; meeting him en route, he encouraged him, saying, "You never betrayed the trust I placed in you; that is why I heeded Hasan and have called you back to office."

sentences.zh: 」未幾，升左丞。

translations.literal: " Before long he was promoted to Left Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: " Before long he was promoted to Left Chancellor.

sentences.zh: 帝崩，英宗宅憂，右丞相帖木迭兒用事，日誅大臣不附己者，中外洶洶。

translations.literal: When the Emperor died, Yingzong was in mourning residence; Right Chancellor Temuder held power and daily executed great ministers who would not submit to him, and alarm spread within and without the court.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor died, Yingzong was in mourning; Right Chancellor Temuder seized power and day by day executed ministers who would not bow to him, until alarm spread through court and realm alike.

sentences.zh: 思明諫曰：「山陵甫畢，新君未立，丞相恣行殺戮，國人皆謂陰有不臣之心。

translations.literal: Siming remonstrated, saying, "The imperial tomb has only just been completed and the new ruler is not yet established; the Chancellor indulges in killing at will, and the people all say he harbors a secret intent of disloyalty."
translations.idiomatic: Siming admonished him: "The imperial tomb rites have only just ended and the new sovereign is not yet enthroned; yet the Chancellor kills at will, and the people whisper that he secretly harbors treasonous intent."

sentences.zh: 萬一諸王駙馬疑而不至，將奈之何？

translations.literal: If by chance the princes and imperial sons-in-law grow suspicious and do not come, what then will you do?
translations.idiomatic: If the princes and imperial sons-in-law grow suspicious and refuse to attend, what then will you do?

sentences.zh: 不可不熟慮也。

translations.literal: This cannot be considered without thorough deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: You must think this through carefully.

sentences.zh: 」眾皆危之，帖木迭兒大悟曰：「非左丞言，幾誤吾事。

translations.literal: " All thought him in peril, but Temuder came to a great awakening and said, "Had it not been for the Left Chancellor's words, I would nearly have ruined my own affairs."
translations.idiomatic: " Everyone feared for Siming, but Temuder was deeply shaken and said, "Had the Left Chancellor not spoken, I would nearly have ruined everything."

sentences.zh: 」帝造壽安山寺，監察御史觀音保、瑣咬兒哈的迷失、成珪、李謙亨強諫，帝震怒，殺觀音保、瑣咬兒哈的迷失，以成珪、李謙亨屬吏，思明白丞相曰：「言事，御史職也，祖宗已來，未嘗殺諫臣。

translations.literal: " The Emperor built Shou'an Temple; investigating censors Guanyinbao, Suoya'er Hadishilishi, Cheng Gui, and Li Qianheng remonstrated forcefully. The Emperor was enraged and executed Guanyinbao and Suoya'er Hadishilishi, handing Cheng Gui and Li Qianheng over to the judicial authorities. Siming told the Chancellor plainly, "To speak on affairs of state is the censor's duty; since the founding of the dynasty, remonstrating officials have never been put to death."
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor undertook construction of Shou'an Temple. Investigating censors Guanyinbao, Suoya'er Hadishilishi, Cheng Gui, and Li Qianheng remonstrated forcefully. The Emperor flew into a rage, executed Guanyinbao and Suoya'er Hadishilishi, and handed Cheng and Li over to the judicial authorities. Siming told the Chancellor plainly, "Speaking on state affairs is a censor's duty; since our ancestors' time, no remonstrating official has been killed."

sentences.zh: 」成、李既屬吏，當論法，丞相乃力言之，二人得從輕典。

translations.literal: " Once Cheng and Li had been handed to the authorities they should have been judged by law; the Chancellor then spoke forcefully on their behalf, and the two received lenient punishment.
translations.idiomatic: " Once Cheng and Li were in custody they should have been tried under law; the Chancellor then spoke forcefully for them, and both received lighter sentences.

sentences.zh: 及拜住為左丞相，與帖木迭兒各樹朋黨，賊害忠良，思明懼禍及，累表辭，不獲，後竟誣以不支蒙古子女口糧，餓死四百人，遂廢於家，杜門六年。

translations.literal: When Bayiju became Left Chancellor, he and Temuder each formed factions and harmed loyal men; Siming feared disaster would reach him and repeatedly submitted memorials to resign but was not permitted. Later he was falsely accused of failing to supply grain rations for Mongol men, women, and children, with four hundred said to have starved to death; he was then dismissed and lived at home behind closed doors for six years.
translations.idiomatic: When Bayiju became Left Chancellor, he and Temuder each built factions and destroyed loyal officials. Siming feared he would be swept up in the purge and repeatedly asked to resign, without success. He was eventually framed for failing to issue grain rations to Mongol households, with four hundred said to have starved; dismissed from office, he kept his doors shut for six years.

sentences.zh: 思明平生不治產，不畜財，收書三萬七千餘卷；

translations.literal: Throughout his life Siming did not manage estates or hoard wealth; he collected more than thirty-seven thousand volumes of books;
translations.idiomatic: Throughout his life Siming neither managed property nor hoarded wealth; he amassed more than thirty-seven thousand volumes of books;

sentences.zh: 尤明於律，與謝仲和、曹鼎新同稱三絕。

translations.literal: he was especially expert in law and, together with Xie Zhonghe and Cao Dingxin, was known as one of the Three Unrivaled.
translations.idiomatic: and was especially masterful in law; together with Xie Zhonghe and Cao Dingxin he was acclaimed as one of the Three Unrivaled.

sentences.zh: 贈推忠翊治守義功臣，依前中書左丞、上護軍、清河郡公，諡貞敏。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted the title Meritorious Minister Who Promotes Loyalty, Assists Governance, and Upholds Righteousness, retaining his former ranks as Left Chancellor of the Secretariat, Senior Guardian General, and Duke of Qinghe, with the posthumous name Zhenmin.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was honored as Meritorious Minister Who Promotes Loyalty, Assists Governance, and Upholds Righteousness, with his former titles of Left Chancellor of the Secretariat, Senior Guardian General, and Duke of Qinghe restored, and the posthumous name Zhenmin.

sentences.zh: ○吳元珪

translations.literal: ○ Wu Yuangui
translations.idiomatic: ○ Wu Yuangui

sentences.zh: 吳元珪，字君璋，廣平人。

translations.literal: Wu Yuangui, styled Junzhang, was a native of Guangping.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Yuangui, whose style name was Junzhang, came from Guangping.

sentences.zh: 父鼎，燕南提刑按察副使。

translations.literal: His father Ding was vice commissioner of the Yannan Circuit for Punishment and Investigation.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ding had served as vice commissioner of the Yannan Circuit for Punishment and Investigation.

sentences.zh: 元珪簡重，好深沉之思，凡徵謀治法、律令章程，皆得於家庭之所授受。

translations.literal: Yuangui was reserved and weighty in manner and loved deep reflection; all matters of policy, law, and regulation he had received within the family.
translations.idiomatic: Yuangui was grave and reserved, fond of deep reflection; everything he knew of statecraft, statutes, and regulations he had learned at home.

sentences.zh: 至元十四年，世祖召見，命侍左右，授後衛經歷，佩金符。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Zhiyuan Kublai summoned him, ordered him to attend at his side, appointed him registrar of the Rear Guard, and bestowed a gold tally.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of Zhiyuan Kublai received him in audience, kept him at his side, appointed him registrar of the Rear Guard, and granted him a gold tally.

sentences.zh: 十七年，從幸上都，受命取禦藥於大都萬歲山，元珪乘傳，未盡一晝夜而至。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he accompanied the Emperor to Shangdu and was ordered to fetch imperial medicine from Wansui Mountain in Dadu; Yuangui traveled by relay post and arrived in less than a day and night.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he accompanied the court to Shangdu and was dispatched to fetch imperial medicine from Wansui Mountain in Dadu; traveling by relay, he arrived in less than a full day and night.

sentences.zh: 帝奇其速，擢樞密都事，升經歷。

translations.literal: The Emperor marveled at his speed and promoted him to director of the Bureau of Military Affairs, then advanced him to registrar.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor marveled at his speed, promoted him to director of the Bureau of Military Affairs, and then advanced him to registrar.

sentences.zh: 嘗從同知樞密院事俺伯進西蕃鎧甲，帝問其制度，元珪應對詳明，帝益奇之。

translations.literal: Once he followed Vice Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs Anbo in presenting Western Regions armor; when the Emperor asked about its design, Yuangui answered in full detail, and the Emperor was all the more impressed.
translations.idiomatic: Once he accompanied Vice Director Anbo in presenting Tibetan armor; when the Emperor asked about its design, Yuangui answered with precision, and the Emperor admired him all the more.

sentences.zh: 初，江南既定，樞密奏裁定官屬，京師五衛、行省、萬戶府設官有差，均俸祿，給醫藥，設學校，置屯田，多元珪所論建。

translations.literal: When the south of the Yangtze was first pacified, the Bureau of Military Affairs memorialized to fix official establishments: the five guards of the capital, branch secretariats, and ten-thousand-household offices were to have differentiated posts, equalized salaries, provision of medicine, establishment of schools, and founding of garrison farms—most of these were proposals Yuangui had advanced.
translations.idiomatic: When the south was first pacified, the Bureau of Military Affairs memorialized to fix official establishments for the five capital guards, branch secretariats, and ten-thousand-household offices—equalizing pay, supplying medicine, founding schools, and establishing garrison farms—most of which Yuangui had proposed.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，參議樞密院事。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he became deliberator of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year he became deliberator of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 時繕修宮城，尚書省奏役軍士萬人，留守司主之。

translations.literal: At that time the palace city was being repaired; the Secretariat memorialized to conscript ten thousand soldiers, with the capital garrison command in charge.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the palace was under repair; the Secretariat proposed conscripting ten thousand soldiers under the capital garrison command.

sentences.zh: 元珪亟陳其不便，乃立武衛，繕理宮城，以留守段天祐兼都指揮使，凡有興作，必以聞於樞府。

translations.literal: Yuangui urgently stated the inconveniences of this plan; thereupon the Martial Guard was established to repair the palace city, with capital garrison commander Duan Tianyou also serving as commander-in-chief; all construction had to be reported to the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Yuangui urgently protested the plan's drawbacks; the Martial Guard was then established to handle palace repairs, with garrison commander Duan Tianyou also serving as commander-in-chief, and all construction had to be reported to the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 尋升樞密院判官。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to vice director of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was promoted to vice director of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 奏定萬戶用軍士八人，千戶四人，百戶二人，多役者有罰。

translations.literal: He memorialized fixing the use of soldiers at eight per ten-thousand-household office, four per thousand-household office, and two per hundred-household office, with penalties for excessive conscription.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized fixing troop quotas at eight soldiers per ten-thousand-household office, four per thousand-household office, and two per hundred-household office, with penalties for over-conscription.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，除禮部侍郎，遷左司郎中。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year he was appointed vice minister of the Ministry of Rites and transferred to director of the Left Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year he was appointed vice minister of Rites and transferred to director of the Left Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 三十一年，參議中書省事。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year he became deliberator of Secretariat affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-first year he became deliberator of Secretariat affairs.

sentences.zh: 大德元年，除吏部尚書。

translations.literal: In the first year of Dade he was appointed Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Dade he was appointed Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 選曹銓注，多有私其鄉里者，元珪曰：「此風不可長，川黨、朔黨之興，宋之所由衰也。

translations.literal: In the appointment bureau many favored their own home districts in nominations; Yuangui said, "This practice must not be allowed to grow; the rise of Sichuan and Shanxi factions was how the Song declined."
translations.idiomatic: In the appointment bureau many favored their own home districts; Yuangui said, "This must not be indulged—the rise of Sichuan and Shanxi factions was how the Song fell."

sentences.zh: 」請謁悉皆謝絕。

translations.literal: " He declined all private petitions.
translations.idiomatic: " He turned away every private solicitation.

sentences.zh: 三年，宣撫燕南，劾貪吏若干人。

translations.literal: In the third year he was sent to pacify and inspect Yannan and impeached several corrupt officials.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was dispatched to pacify and inspect Yannan and impeached several corrupt officials.

sentences.zh: 遷工部尚書，河朔連年水旱，五穀不登，元珪言：「《春秋》之義，以養民為本，凡用民力者必書，蓋民力息則生養遂，生養遂則教化行而風俗美。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of Works. The north of the Yellow River had suffered flood and drought for successive years and the five grains did not ripen; Yuangui said, "The meaning of the Spring and Autumn Annals takes nourishing the people as fundamental; wherever the people's labor is used it must be recorded, for when the people's strength rests, sustenance flourishes, and when sustenance flourishes, instruction spreads and customs become fine."
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Minister of Works. North of the Yellow River had suffered flood and drought year after year, and the harvests failed; Yuangui said, "The Spring and Autumn Annals teach that nourishing the people comes first; every levy on their labor must be recorded, for when the people rest, livelihoods thrive, and when livelihoods thrive, instruction spreads and customs improve."

sentences.zh: 」宰相嘉其言，土木之工稍為之息。

translations.literal: " The chancellor praised his words, and construction projects were somewhat reduced.
translations.idiomatic: " The chancellor praised his counsel, and construction projects were scaled back.

sentences.zh: 六年，僉河南行中書省事，將行，拜江浙行省參知政事。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was appointed to the Henan Branch Secretariat and was about to depart when he was appointed Vice Director of the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was appointed to the Henan Branch Secretariat; before he could depart, he was named Vice Director of the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 初，硃清、張瑄以財雄江南，遍以金幣連結當路，及伏誅，錄其家，具籍所交諸公貴人，而江浙省臣為尤甚，惟元珪一無所污。

translations.literal: Earlier Zhu Qing and Zhang Xuan had dominated the wealth of the south with gold and coin linking all those in power; when they were executed their households were inventoried and a full register made of the great nobles they had cultivated—among whom officials of the Jiang-Zhe province were especially numerous—yet Yuangui alone had not been tainted.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Zhu Qing and Zhang Xuan had dominated Jiangnan's wealth, buying influence with gold throughout the bureaucracy; when they were executed, their households were inventoried and every official they had cultivated was listed—the Jiang-Zhe provincial staff especially—yet Yuangui alone had taken nothing.

sentences.zh: 武宗即位，由僉樞密院事拜樞密副使。

translations.literal: When Wuzong took the throne, from his post in the Bureau of Military Affairs he was appointed Vice Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Wuzong came to the throne, Yuangui rose from his post in the Bureau of Military Affairs to Vice Director of that bureau.

sentences.zh: 詔元珪二十餘人議政中書，若惜人力，嚴選舉，節財用，定律令，謹賞罰，建科舉，課農桑，汰冗員，易封贈，皆切於世務者。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Yuangui and more than twenty others to deliberate on government at the Secretariat—such matters as sparing human labor, tightening selection, economizing expenditures, fixing statutes, careful rewards and punishments, establishing the civil service examinations, encouraging agriculture and sericulture, eliminating redundant posts, and reforming enfeoffment and posthumous honors—all pressing affairs of state.
translations.idiomatic: An edict summoned Yuangui and more than twenty others to deliberate on governance at the Secretariat—sparing labor, tightening appointments, economizing expenditures, fixing statutes, careful rewards and punishments, restoring examinations, promoting agriculture, cutting redundant posts, reforming enfeoffments—all matters urgent to the realm.

sentences.zh: 初，詔發軍萬人屯田稱海以實邊，海都之亂，被俘者眾，至是頗有來歸者，飢寒不能存，至鬻子以活。

translations.literal: Earlier an edict had sent ten thousand troops to garrison and farm at Chenghai to strengthen the border; in Haidu's rebellion many were captured, and by this time quite a few had returned but, unable to survive hunger and cold, even sold their children to live.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier an edict had sent ten thousand troops to farm at Chenghai and strengthen the frontier; in Haidu's rebellion many were taken captive, and by now a good number had returned but, starving and freezing, some even sold their children to survive.

sentences.zh: 元珪具其事以聞，詔賜錢贖之。

translations.literal: Yuangui reported the matter in full and an edict granted money to redeem them.
translations.idiomatic: Yuangui reported the full situation, and an edict granted funds to redeem the children.

sentences.zh: 帝在軍中，即聞元珪名，至是，特加平章政事，賜白金二百五十兩、只孫衣四襲。

translations.literal: While still in the army the Emperor had already heard Yuangui's name; at this time he was specially advanced to Director of the Secretariat and granted two hundred fifty taels of white gold and four sets of zhisun robes.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor had heard Yuangui's name while still campaigning; now he was specially promoted to Director of the Secretariat and granted two hundred fifty taels of white gold and four sets of zhisun robes.

sentences.zh: 仁宗即位，詔元珪與十六人議時政。

translations.literal: When Renzong took the throne, an edict ordered Yuangui and sixteen others to deliberate on current policy.
translations.idiomatic: When Renzong came to the throne, an edict ordered Yuangui and sixteen others to deliberate on current affairs.

sentences.zh: 皇慶元年，出拜江浙行省左丞。

translations.literal: In the first year of Huangqing he was sent out as Left Chancellor of the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Huangqing he was posted out as Left Chancellor of the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 江淮漕臣言：「江南殷富，蓋由多匿腴田，若再行檢覆之法，當益田畝累萬計。

translations.literal: The grain transport official of the Jiang-Huai region said, "The wealth of the south comes largely from hiding fertile fields; if the method of re-inspection were applied again, field acreage would increase by tens of thousands."
translations.idiomatic: The Jiang-Huai grain transport official said, "Jiangnan's prosperity owes much to concealed fertile land; if we reapply the inspection method, registered acreage will rise by tens of thousands."

sentences.zh: 」元珪曰：「江南之平，幾四十年，戶有定籍，田有定畝，一有動搖，其害不細。

translations.literal: " Yuangui said, "The south has been pacified for nearly forty years; households have fixed registers and fields fixed acreage—once this is disturbed, the harm will not be slight."
translations.idiomatic: " Yuangui replied, "The south has been at peace for nearly forty years; households have fixed registers and fields fixed acreage. Disturb that, and the harm will be grave."

sentences.zh: 」執其論固爭，月餘不能止，移疾去。

translations.literal: " He held to his view and argued firmly for more than a month without stopping them; he then submitted notice of illness and left office.
translations.idiomatic: " He held firm to his view and argued for more than a month without prevailing, then pleaded illness and resigned.

sentences.zh: 延祐元年，拜甘肅行省左丞。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yanyou he was appointed Left Chancellor of the Gansu Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yanyou he was appointed Left Chancellor of the Gansu Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，召還，俾宣撫遼陽諸郡，復為樞密副使，召見嘉禧殿，帝曰：「卿先朝舊臣，宜在舊服。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was recalled, sent to pacify and inspect the commanderies of Liaoyang, and again made Vice Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs; summoned to Jiaxi Hall, the Emperor said, "You are an old minister of the previous reign and should resume your former post."
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year he was recalled, dispatched to pacify and inspect the Liaoyang commanderies, and restored as Vice Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs. Summoned to Jiaxi Hall, the Emperor said, "You are a veteran of the previous reign and belong in your former station."

sentences.zh: 」特加榮祿大夫，賜鈔五千緡、貂裘二襲。

translations.literal: " He was specially advanced to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and granted five thousand strings of paper money and two sable fur coats.
translations.idiomatic: " He was specially advanced to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and granted five thousand strings of paper money and two sable fur coats.

sentences.zh: 元珪奏曰：「昔世祖限田四百畝，以給軍需，餘田悉貢賦稅。

translations.literal: Yuangui memorialized, saying, "Formerly Kublai limited fields to four hundred mu for military supply, and all remaining fields paid tribute and tax."
translations.idiomatic: Yuangui memorialized: "Formerly Kublai limited each holding to four hundred mu for military supply; all land beyond that paid tribute and tax."

sentences.zh: 今經理江淮田土，第以增金為能，加以有司頭會箕斂，俾元元之民，困苦日甚，臣恐變生不測，非國之福，惟陛下少加意焉。

translations.literal: Now in administering the fields of the Jiang-Huai region, merit is measured only by increased revenue; moreover officials levy by the scoop and rake, so that the common people grow daily more distressed. I fear unforeseen disturbances may arise—this is no blessing to the state—and I beg Your Majesty to give the matter some attention.
translations.idiomatic: Now in surveying Jiang-Huai land, officials are judged solely by how much revenue they raise; on top of that they squeeze the people dry, and the common folk grow more wretched by the day. I fear unrest may break out without warning—this bodes ill for the state—and beg Your Majesty to take heed.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「凡爾軍士之田，並遵舊制。」

translations.literal: " The Emperor said, "All fields of you soldiers shall follow the old regulations."
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor said, "All fields held by soldiers shall follow the old regulations."

sentences.zh: 至治元年，英宗即位，元珪與知樞密院事帖木兒不花上軍民之政十餘事，大抵言：諸王近侍，不可干軍政；

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhizhi, when Yingzong took the throne, Yuangui together with Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs Temur-Buqa presented more than ten items on military and civil administration, saying in general that princes and close attendants must not interfere in military affairs;
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhizhi, when Yingzong came to the throne, Yuangui and Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs Temur-Buqa submitted more than ten proposals on military and civil administration, chief among them that princes and close attendants must not meddle in military affairs;

sentences.zh: 管軍官吏，不可漁取軍戶；

translations.literal: officers administering troops must not plunder military households;
translations.idiomatic: officers in charge of troops must not prey on military households;

sentences.zh: 軍官之材者，當遷其職；

translations.literal: capable military officers should be transferred to appropriate posts;
translations.idiomatic: capable military officers should be moved to posts that suit their talents;

sentences.zh: 有司賦役，當務均一，而軍民不可有所偏；

translations.literal: official levies and corvée should strive for uniformity, and soldiers and civilians must not be treated with partiality;
translations.idiomatic: official levies and labor service must be kept uniform, with no favoritism between soldiers and civilians;

sentences.zh: 軍官襲職，惟傳嫡嗣，而支庶不可有所亂。

translations.literal: succession in military office should pass only to the legitimate heir, and collateral lines must not be allowed to confuse the order.
translations.idiomatic: military offices should pass only to legitimate heirs, and collateral lines must not be allowed to disrupt succession.

sentences.zh: 帝並嘉納，即降旨施行之。

translations.literal: The Emperor approved all and immediately issued edicts to put them into effect.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor approved them all and immediately issued edicts to carry them out.

sentences.zh: 元珪以年老致仕，至治二年，起商議中書省事。

translations.literal: Yuangui retired on account of age; in the second year of Zhizhi he was recalled to deliberate on Secretariat affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Yuangui had retired on account of age; in the second year of Zhizhi he was recalled to deliberate on Secretariat affairs.

sentences.zh: 三年卒。

translations.literal: In the third year he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he died.

sentences.zh: 泰定元年，贈光祿大夫、河南等處行省平章政事、柱國，追封趙國公，諡忠簡。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taiding he was posthumously granted Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Director of the Henan Branch Secretariat, and Pillar of the State, posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Zhao with the posthumous name Zhongjian.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Taiding he was posthumously honored as Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Director of the Henan Branch Secretariat, and Pillar of the State, enfeoffed posthumously as Duke of Zhao with the posthumous name Zhongjian.

sentences.zh: 三年，復加推誠佐理功臣、光祿大夫、司徒。

translations.literal: In the third year he was further granted Meritorious Minister Who Promotes Sincerity and Assists Governance, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was further honored as Meritorious Minister Who Promotes Sincerity and Assists Governance, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: ○張昇

translations.literal: ○ Zhang Sheng
translations.idiomatic: ○ Zhang Sheng

sentences.zh: 張昇，字伯高，其先定州人，後徙平州。

translations.literal: Zhang Sheng, styled Bogao, was originally from Dingzhou; his family later moved to Pingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Sheng, whose style name was Bogao, came from Dingzhou by ancestry but later settled in Pingzhou.

sentences.zh: 升幼警敏過人，學語時，輒能辨字音，應對異於常兒；

translations.literal: As a child Sheng was exceptionally quick-witted; when learning to speak he could distinguish character sounds and his replies differed from ordinary children;
translations.idiomatic: As a boy Sheng was unusually quick-witted; even while learning to speak he could distinguish character sounds, and his replies set him apart from other children;

sentences.zh: 既長，力學，工文辭。

translations.literal: when grown he studied diligently and excelled in literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: when he grew up he studied hard and became skilled in literary composition.

sentences.zh: 至元二十九年，用薦者授將仕郎、翰林國史院編修官，預修《世祖實錄》。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year of Zhiyuan, on recommendation he was appointed Gentleman for Merit and compiler at the Hanlin Academy National History Office, taking part in compiling the Veritable Records of Shizu.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year of Zhiyuan, on recommendation he was appointed Gentleman for Merit and compiler at the Hanlin National History Office, helping compile the Veritable Records of Kublai.

sentences.zh: 升應奉翰林文字，尋升修撰，歷興文署令，遷太常博士。

translations.literal: Sheng served as Hanlin literary attendant, was soon promoted to compiler, served as director of the Bureau for Promoting Literature, and was transferred to erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng served as Hanlin literary attendant, was soon promoted to compiler, directed the Bureau for Promoting Literature, and became an erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 成宗崩，大臣承中旨，議奉徽號，饗宗廟，升曰：「在故典，凡有事於宗廟，必書嗣皇帝名，今將何書？

translations.literal: When Chengzong died, great ministers acting on the inner court's intent discussed offering a posthumous title and sacrifices at the ancestral temple. Sheng said, "According to former statutes, whenever there is an affair at the ancestral temple, the name of the succeeding emperor must be recorded—what name shall be written now?"
translations.idiomatic: When Chengzong died, senior ministers acting on the inner court's wishes debated a posthumous title and ancestral sacrifices. Sheng asked, "Under former statutes, any ancestral temple rite must record the succeeding emperor's name—whose name should we write now?"

sentences.zh: 」議遂寢。

translations.literal: " The discussion was then dropped.
translations.idiomatic: " The proposal was dropped.

sentences.zh: 武宗即位，議躬祀禮，升據經引古，參酌時宜以對，帝嘉納之。

translations.literal: When Wuzong took the throne, the personal performance of sacrificial rites was debated; Sheng answered by citing the classics and ancient precedents and weighing present circumstances, and the Emperor praised and accepted his view.
translations.idiomatic: When Wuzong came to the throne, the court debated whether the emperor should perform sacrifices in person; Sheng answered with classical citations and ancient precedent, adjusted to the times, and the Emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 至大初，改太常寺為太常禮儀院，即除升為判官。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhida the Court of Imperial Sacrifices was changed to the Court of Imperial Sacrificial Rites, and Sheng was immediately appointed its vice director.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhida reign the Court of Imperial Sacrifices was reorganized as the Court of Imperial Sacrificial Rites, and Sheng was immediately named its vice director.

sentences.zh: 久之，外補知汝寧府。

translations.literal: After a long while he was posted outside the capital as prefect of Runing.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was posted outside the capital as prefect of Runing.

sentences.zh: 民有告寄束書於其家者，逾三年取閱，有禁書一編，且記里中大家姓名於上，升亟呼吏焚其書，曰：「妄言誣民，且再更赦矣，勿論。

translations.literal: A man reported that someone had left a bundle of books at his house; after more than three years he opened it and found a volume of banned books with the names of leading local families recorded in it. Sheng immediately ordered an official to burn the book, saying, "This is reckless talk to frame the people, and there have already been two general amnesties—do not pursue it."
translations.idiomatic: A man reported that someone had left a bundle of books at his house; more than three years later he opened it and found banned writings listing the names of prominent local families. Sheng immediately ordered the book burned, saying, "This is a frame-up, and there have already been two general amnesties—let the matter drop."

sentences.zh: 」同列懼，皆引起。

translations.literal: " His colleagues were afraid and all rose to leave.
translations.idiomatic: " His colleagues were alarmed and all rose to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 既而事聞，廷議謂升脫姦軌，遣使窮問，卒無跡可指，乃詰以擅焚書狀，升對曰：「事固類姦軌，然升備位郡守，為民父母，今斥誣訴，免冤濫，雖重得罪不避。

translations.literal: When the matter became known, court discussion held that Sheng had shielded a conspiracy and sent envoys to investigate thoroughly; in the end no trace could be found, and he was questioned about burning the book on his own authority. Sheng replied, "The affair indeed resembled a conspiracy, yet I hold the post of prefect and am parent to the people; to reject false accusations and spare wrongful punishment—even if I must bear a heavy penalty I will not shrink from it."
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the court, ministers accused Sheng of shielding sedition and sent investigators; finding no evidence, they charged him with burning the book on his own authority. Sheng replied, "It did look like sedition, but as prefect I am parent to the people; to reject a false accusation and spare the innocent—even at the cost of severe punishment—I would not shrink from that."

sentences.zh: 」乃坐奪俸二月。

translations.literal: " He was sentenced to forfeiture of salary for two months.
translations.idiomatic: " He was sentenced to two months' forfeiture of salary.

sentences.zh: 旁郡移文報吳人侯君遠者言：「歲直壬子六月朔日蝕，其占為兵寇；

translations.literal: A neighboring prefecture sent a dispatch reporting that a man of Wu named Hou Junyuan said, "In the year of the stem-branch cycle renzi, on the first day of the sixth month there will be an eclipse; the omen is military invasion;"
translations.idiomatic: A neighboring prefecture reported that a Wu man named Hou Junyuan claimed, "In the renzi year, on the first day of the sixth month there will be an eclipse—a portent of war;"

sentences.zh: 歲癸丑，其應在吳分野。

translations.literal: in the year guichou the fulfillment will fall in the celestial domain of Wu."
translations.idiomatic: in the guichou year the omen will fall upon the Wu region."

sentences.zh: 」同列欲召屬縣為備禦計，升曰：「此訛言，久當自息，毋用惑民聽。

translations.literal: " His colleagues wished to summon the subordinate counties to prepare defenses; Sheng said, "This is false rumor; in time it will die of itself—there is no need to alarm the people."
translations.idiomatic: " His colleagues wanted to summon the counties to prepare defenses; Sheng said, "This is idle rumor—it will die out on its own; do not alarm the people."

sentences.zh: 」斥其無稽，眾論韙之。

translations.literal: " He rejected it as groundless, and public opinion approved.
translations.idiomatic: " He dismissed it as baseless, and everyone agreed.

sentences.zh: 部使者舉治行為諸郡最。

translations.literal: The ministry envoy cited his governance as the best among the prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry envoy ranked his governance the best among the prefectures.

sentences.zh: 歷江西行省左右司郎中，除紹興路總管。

translations.literal: He served as director of the Left and Right Secretariats of the Jiangxi Branch Secretariat and was appointed circuit intendant of Shaoxing.
translations.idiomatic: He served as director in the Jiangxi Branch Secretariat and was appointed circuit intendant of Shaoxing.

sentences.zh: 初，大德、至大間，越大饑，且疫癘，民死者殆半，賦稅鹽課責里胥代納，吏並緣為奸，害富家，升為證於簿籍，白行省蠲之。

translations.literal: Earlier, between the Dade and Zhida eras, Yue suffered great famine and plague; nearly half the people died. Tax and salt levies were forced on village clerks to pay in proxy, and officials used this as a pretext for corruption, harming wealthy households. Sheng verified the records and reported to the branch secretariat for exemption.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, during the Dade and Zhida reigns, Yue suffered famine and plague until nearly half the population perished. Tax and salt dues were forced onto village clerks, and officials used the scheme to prey on wealthy families. Sheng verified the registers and persuaded the branch secretariat to grant relief.

sentences.zh: 前守有為江浙行省參知政事者，爭代者祿米，有隙，欲內之罪，移平江歲輸海運糧布囊三萬，俾紹興制如數，民患苦之，不能堪。

translations.literal: A former prefect who had become Vice Director of the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat quarreled over substitute salary grain and bore a grudge, wishing to trap Sheng in guilt; he shifted to Shaoxing the annual Pingjiang tribute of thirty thousand sacks of maritime grain cloth, and the people suffered unbearably.
translations.idiomatic: A former prefect who had risen to Vice Director of the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat quarreled with Sheng over substitute salary grain and sought to trap him; he imposed on Shaoxing Pingjiang's annual tribute of thirty thousand sacks of maritime grain cloth, and the people could not bear it.

sentences.zh: 更數守，謂歲例如此，置弗問。

translations.literal: Several succeeding prefects said the annual precedent was thus and left it unaddressed.
translations.idiomatic: Several succeeding prefects accepted it as annual precedent and ignored the burden.

sentences.zh: 升言：「麻非越土所生，海漕實吳郡事，於越無與。

translations.literal: Sheng said, "Hemp is not native to Yue soil; maritime transport is truly a Wu commandery affair and has nothing to do with Yue."
translations.idiomatic: Sheng argued, "Hemp is not grown in Yue; maritime transport is Wu's responsibility and has nothing to do with Shaoxing."

sentences.zh: 」章上，卒罷之。

translations.literal: " When his memorial went up, the levy was finally abolished.
translations.idiomatic: " His memorial prevailed, and the levy was abolished.

sentences.zh: 升既謹於繩吏，又果於去民瘼，故人心悅服。

translations.literal: Sheng was both strict in restraining officials and resolute in removing the people's afflictions, so hearts were pleased and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng was strict with officials and resolute in lifting the people's burdens, and the people came to trust him wholeheartedly.

sentences.zh: 歷湖北道廉訪使、江南行台治書侍御史，召為參議中書省事，改樞密院判官，尋復中書參議。

translations.literal: He served as surveillance commissioner of the Hubei Circuit and investigating censor of the Jiangnan Branch Censorate, was summoned as deliberator of Secretariat affairs, was changed to vice director of the Bureau of Military Affairs, and soon returned as Secretariat deliberator.
translations.idiomatic: He served as surveillance commissioner of Hubei and investigating censor on the Jiangnan Branch Censorate, was summoned as Secretariat deliberator, became vice director of the Bureau of Military Affairs, and soon returned as Secretariat deliberator.

sentences.zh: 至治二年，又出為河東道廉訪使，未行，拜治書侍御史。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhizhi he was again sent out as surveillance commissioner of the Hedong Circuit but did not depart and was appointed investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhizhi he was posted to Hedong as surveillance commissioner but never departed; instead he was appointed investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 明年，出為淮西道廉訪使。

translations.literal: The next year he was sent out as surveillance commissioner of the Huaixi Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was posted as surveillance commissioner of Huaixi.

sentences.zh: 泰定二年，拜陝西行省參知政事，加中奉大夫，尋遷遼東道廉訪使。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taiding he was appointed Vice Director of the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat and advanced to Grand Master for Assisting the Court; soon he was transferred to surveillance commissioner of the Liaodong Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Taiding he was appointed Vice Director of the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat and advanced to Grand Master for Assisting the Court; soon he was transferred to surveillance commissioner of Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 屬永平大水，民多捐瘠，升請發海道糧十八萬石、鈔五萬緡，以賑饑民，且蠲其歲賦，朝廷從之，民得全活者眾。

translations.literal: When Yongping suffered great flood and many people were emaciated, Sheng requested release of one hundred eighty thousand shi of maritime grain and fifty thousand strings of paper money to relieve the starving, and also exemption of the year's tax levy; the court agreed, and many people were preserved alive.
translations.idiomatic: When Yongping was struck by severe flooding and many people were starving, Sheng requested one hundred eighty thousand shi of maritime grain and fifty thousand strings of paper money for relief, plus exemption of that year's taxes; the court agreed, and countless lives were saved.

sentences.zh: 明年，召拜侍御史。

translations.literal: The next year he was summoned and appointed attendant censor.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was summoned as attendant censor.

sentences.zh: 天歷初，出為山東道廉訪使，時方有警，有司請完城以為備，升曰：「民恃吾以生，完城是棄民也。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianli he was sent out as surveillance commissioner of the Shandong Circuit; there was then an alarm, and officials requested repairing the city walls for defense. Sheng said, "The people rely on us for their lives—to repair the walls is to abandon the people."
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianli reign he was posted to Shandong as surveillance commissioner. With unrest abroad, officials proposed repairing the city walls. Sheng said, "The people depend on us for their livelihood—to fortify the walls is to abandon them."

sentences.zh: 」由是民皆安之。

translations.literal: " Thereby the people were all reassured.
translations.idiomatic: " The people were reassured.

sentences.zh: 文宗賜尚醖文幣，以賞其功。

translations.literal: Wenzong granted imperial wine and patterned silks to reward his merit.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzong rewarded him with imperial wine and patterned silks.

sentences.zh: 逾年，召為太禧院副使，兼奉贊神御殿事，除河南省左丞，复遷淮西道廉訪使。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was summoned as Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Blessings, concurrently attending the Spirit Imperial Hall, appointed Left Chancellor of the Henan Province, and again transferred to surveillance commissioner of the Huaixi Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was summoned as Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Blessings, with concurrent duty at the Spirit Imperial Hall, appointed Left Chancellor of Henan Province, and again posted to Huaixi as surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 升時年六十有九，上書乞致仕。

translations.literal: Sheng was then sixty-nine and submitted a memorial requesting retirement.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng was then sixty-nine and petitioned to retire.

sentences.zh: 至順二年，復起為集賢侍講學士，文宗眷待之意甚隆。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhishun he was recalled as lecturer of the Hall of Gathered Worthies; Wenzong's favor toward him was very great.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhishun he was recalled as lecturer of the Hall of Gathered Worthies, and Wenzong treated him with exceptional favor.

sentences.zh: 元統元年，順帝即位，首詔在廷耆艾，訪問治道，升條上時所宜先者十事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuantong, when Shundi took the throne, his first edict summoned the elders at court to inquire about the way of governance; Sheng itemized ten matters that should be prioritized at the time.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yuantong, when Shundi came to the throne, his first edict summoned court elders to advise on governance; Sheng submitted ten priorities for the age.

sentences.zh: 尋兼經筵官，廷試進士，特命升讀卷，事已，告省先墓。

translations.literal: Soon he also served on the Classics Mat lectures; at the palace examination for jinshi he was specially ordered to read the papers; when the affair was finished he asked leave to visit his ancestors' graves.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he also served on the Classics Mat; at the palace examination he was specially assigned to read the papers; when the session ended he asked leave to visit his family's graves.

sentences.zh: 帝賜金織文袍，以寵其歸。

translations.literal: The Emperor granted him a gold-woven patterned robe to honor his departure.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor granted him a gold-woven patterned robe to honor his journey home.

sentences.zh: 明年，以奎章閣大學士、資善大夫、知經筵事召，賜上尊，趣就職，升以疾辭。

translations.literal: The next year he was summoned as Grand Academician of the Kuizhang Pavilion, Grand Master for Assisting Goodness, and director of Classics Mat affairs; he was granted imperial wine and urged to take office, but Sheng declined on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was summoned as Grand Academician of the Kuizhang Pavilion, Grand Master for Assisting Goodness, and director of the Classics Mat; the Emperor granted imperial wine and urged him to serve, but Sheng pleaded illness.

sentences.zh: 帝察其不可強，許之。

translations.literal: The Emperor saw he could not be compelled and consented.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing he could not be pressed, the Emperor consented.

sentences.zh: 尋命本郡月給祿半，以終其身。

translations.literal: Soon he was ordered to receive half salary monthly from his home prefecture for the rest of his life.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was granted half his former salary monthly from his home prefecture for life.

sentences.zh: 至正元年卒，年八十一。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhizheng he died, aged eighty-one.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhizheng he died at the age of eighty-one.

sentences.zh: 贈資德大夫、河南等處行中書省左丞，諡文憲。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Grand Master of Assisting Virtue and Left Chancellor of the Henan Branch Secretariat, with the posthumous name Wenxian.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was honored as Grand Master of Assisting Virtue and Left Chancellor of the Henan Branch Secretariat, with the posthumous name Wenxian.

sentences.zh: 臧夢解陸垕

translations.literal: Zang Mengjie and Lu Hou
translations.idiomatic: Zang Mengjie and Lu Hou

sentences.zh: 臧夢解，慶元人，宋末中進士第，未官而國亡。

translations.literal: Zang Mengjie was a native of Qingyuan; at the end of the Song he passed the jinshi examination but had not yet taken office when the state perished.
translations.idiomatic: Zang Mengjie came from Qingyuan; at the end of the Song he passed the jinshi examination but never took office before the dynasty fell.

sentences.zh: 至元十三年，從其鄉郡守將內附，授奉訓大夫、婺州路軍民人匠提舉。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Zhiyuan he followed his home district's prefect in submitting to the Yuan and was appointed Grand Master for Court Instruction and superintendent of military households and artisans of Wuzhou Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of Zhiyuan he followed his home prefect in submitting to the Yuan and was appointed Grand Master for Court Instruction and superintendent of military households and artisans in Wuzhou Circuit.

sentences.zh: 未幾，例革其所司，而浙東宣慰司舉夢解才兼儒吏，可試州郡，朝廷是之，授息州知州。

translations.literal: Before long his office was abolished by regulation; the Zhedong Pacification Commission recommended Mengjie as talented in both Confucian learning and administration, fit to be tried in a prefecture or district, and the court agreed, appointing him prefect of Xizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before long his office was abolished by regulation; the Zhedong Pacification Commission recommended Mengjie as a scholar-official fit for prefectural trial, the court agreed, and he was appointed prefect of Xizhou.

sentences.zh: 未行，改知海寧州。

translations.literal: Before he departed he was changed to magistrate of Haining Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could depart he was reassigned as magistrate of Haining Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 時淮東按察副使王慶之按行至其州，見夢解剛直廉慎，而學有淵奧，自任職以來，門無私謁，官署蕭然，凡有差役，皆當其貧富，而吏無所預。

translations.literal: At that time Vice Commissioner Wang Qingzhi of the Huaidong Surveillance Commission made an inspection tour to the prefecture and saw that Mengjie was upright, incorruptible, and cautious, with learning of profound depth; since taking office there had been no private callers at his gate and the government offices were austere; all corvée assignments were apportioned according to wealth, and clerks had no part in it.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Vice Commissioner Wang Qingzhi of Huaidong Surveillance toured the prefecture and found Mengjie upright, incorruptible, and learned in depth; since taking office his gate had admitted no private callers, his offices were austere, corvée was assigned according to wealth, and clerks had no hand in it.

sentences.zh: 於是民以戶計者，新增七百六十有四；

translations.literal: thereupon households registered by count increased by seven hundred sixty-four;
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon registered households increased by seven hundred sixty-four;

sentences.zh: 田以頃計者，新辟四百四十有三；

translations.literal: fields reckoned in qing newly opened by four hundred forty-three;
translations.idiomatic: newly opened fields increased by four hundred forty-three qing;

sentences.zh: 桑柘榆柳，交廕境內，而政平訟簡，為諸州縣最。

translations.literal: mulberry, catalpa, elm, and willow shaded the borders within, government was tranquil and lawsuits few, and it was foremost among prefectures and districts.
translations.idiomatic: mulberry, catalpa, elm, and willow shaded the countryside; government was tranquil and lawsuits few, and Haining ranked first among prefectures and districts.

sentences.zh: 乃舉夢解才德兼備，宜擢清要，以展所蘊。

translations.literal: He then recommended Mengjie as possessing both talent and virtue, fit for promotion to a key post to display his endowments.
translations.idiomatic: He recommended Mengjie as possessing both talent and virtue, fit for promotion to a key post where his gifts could be fully used.

sentences.zh: 而御史臺亦以其廉能，抗章薦之。

translations.literal: The Censorate also, for his integrity and ability, submitted a memorial recommending him.
translations.idiomatic: The Censorate also memorialized recommending him for his integrity and ability.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，夢解滿去者至是已五年矣。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year, five years had passed since Mengjie's term had ended.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year, five years had passed since Mengjie completed his term.

sentences.zh: 屬江陰飢，江浙行省委夢解賑之。

translations.literal: When Jiangyin suffered famine, the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat commissioned Mengjie to relieve it.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiangyin suffered famine, the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat commissioned Mengjie to administer relief.

sentences.zh: 夢解不為文具，皆躬至其地，而人給以米，所活四萬五千餘人。

translations.literal: Mengjie did not make empty documents but personally went to each place and gave rice per person, preserving more than forty-five thousand lives.
translations.idiomatic: Mengjie dispensed with paperwork, went to each place in person, and distributed rice per head, saving more than forty-five thousand lives.

sentences.zh: 江南行台治書侍御史苟宗道，聞而韙之，舉其名上聞，除同知桂陽路總管府事。

translations.literal: Gou Zongdao, investigating censor of the Jiangnan Branch Censorate, heard and approved, reported his name upward, and Mengjie was appointed Associate Administrator of the Guiyang Circuit Intendant's Office.
translations.idiomatic: Gou Zongdao, investigating censor on the Jiangnan Branch Censorate, heard of this and approved; he reported Mengjie's name to the throne, and Mengjie was appointed Associate Administrator of Guiyang Circuit.

sentences.zh: 三十年，擢奉議大夫、廣西肅政廉訪副使。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year he was promoted to Grand Master for Discussion and Vice Surveillance Commissioner of Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year he was promoted to Grand Master for Discussion and Vice Surveillance Commissioner of Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 故事，煙瘴之地，行部者多不躬至，而夢解咸遍歷焉。

translations.literal: By precedent, in malarial regions touring officials often did not go in person, but Mengjie visited them all.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent, surveillance officials often avoided malarial regions in person, but Mengjie toured every one of them.

sentences.zh: 遂按問賓州、藤州兩路達魯花赤，與凡貪官姦吏，置於法者無慮八十餘人。

translations.literal: He then investigated the darughachi of the Binzhou and Tengzhou circuits and all corrupt and wicked officials; those punished by law numbered no fewer than eighty.
translations.idiomatic: He investigated the darughachi of Binzhou and Tengzhou circuits and every corrupt official; more than eighty were punished by law.

sentences.zh: 又平反邕州黃震被誣贓罪，及藤州唐氏婦被誣殺夫罪，凡兩冤獄。

translations.literal: He also righted two wrongful cases: Huang Zhen of Yongzhou falsely accused of embezzlement, and a Tang woman of Tengzhou falsely accused of murdering her husband.
translations.idiomatic: He also cleared two wrongful convictions: Huang Zhen of Yongzhou, falsely accused of embezzlement, and a Mrs. Tang of Tengzhou, falsely accused of murdering her husband.

sentences.zh: 大德元年，遷江西肅政廉訪副使。

translations.literal: In the first year of Dade he was transferred to Vice Surveillance Commissioner of Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Dade he was transferred to Vice Surveillance Commissioner of Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 有臨江路總管李倜，素狡獪，而又附大臣勢，以控持省憲，夢解按其贓罪，而一道澄清。

translations.literal: There was circuit intendant Li Tong of Linjiang, by nature cunning and relying on great ministers' power to control the provincial surveillance apparatus; Mengjie prosecuted his embezzlement and the whole circuit was cleared.
translations.idiomatic: Li Tong, circuit intendant of Linjiang, was cunning by nature and used great ministers' influence to control provincial surveillance; Mengjie prosecuted his embezzlement and the whole circuit was cleansed.

sentences.zh: 六年，遷浙東肅政廉訪副使。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was transferred to Vice Surveillance Commissioner of Zhedong.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was transferred to Vice Surveillance Commissioner of Zhedong.

sentences.zh: 九年，除廣東肅政廉訪使。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was appointed Surveillance Commissioner of Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was appointed Surveillance Commissioner of Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 夢解至是，既老且病，乃納祿退居杭州，以亞中大夫、湖南宣慰副使致仕。

translations.literal: By this time Mengjie was both old and ill; he surrendered his salary and retired to Hangzhou, retiring with the ranks of Subordinate Grand Master and Vice Pacification Commissioner of Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: By then Mengjie was old and ill; he surrendered his salary and retired to Hangzhou, with the ranks of Subordinate Grand Master and Vice Pacification Commissioner of Hunan.

sentences.zh: 後至元元年卒。

translations.literal: In the first year of the Later Zhiyuan era he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Later Zhiyuan era he died.

sentences.zh: 夢解博學洽聞，為時名儒，然不少迂腐，而敏於政事，其操守尤為介特。

translations.literal: Mengjie was broadly learned and well informed, a famous Confucian of the age, yet not at all pedantic; he was keen in government affairs, and his integrity was especially uncompromising.
translations.idiomatic: Mengjie was broadly learned and renowned as a Confucian of his age, yet not pedantic; he was sharp in administration, and his integrity was especially uncompromising.

sentences.zh: 所著書，有《周官考》三卷、《春秋微》一卷。

translations.literal: Among his writings are three juan of Examination of the Offices of Zhou and one juan of Subtleties of the Spring and Autumn Annals.
translations.idiomatic: His writings include three juan of Examination of the Offices of Zhou and one juan of Subtleties of the Spring and Autumn Annals.

sentences.zh: 夢解嘗自號魯山大夫，士之稱之者，不以官，皆曰魯山先生云。

translations.literal: Mengjie once styled himself the Grandee of Lushan; scholars who spoke of him did not use his office title but all called him Master Lushan.
translations.idiomatic: Mengjie styled himself the Grandee of Lushan; scholars who spoke of him ignored his official titles and called him Master Lushan.

sentences.zh: 同時有陸垕者，與夢解齊名。

translations.literal: At the same time there was Lu Hou, equally famous with Mengjie.
translations.idiomatic: At the same time there was Lu Hou, equally renowned with Mengjie.

sentences.zh: 監察御史鄭鵬南嘗以二人並薦於朝。

translations.literal: Investigating censor Zheng Pengnan once recommended both men together to the court.
translations.idiomatic: Investigating censor Zheng Pengnan once recommended both men together to the court.

sentences.zh: 垕字仁重，江陰人也。

translations.literal: Hou, styled Renzhong, was a native of Jiangyin.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Hou, whose style name was Renzhong, came from Jiangyin.

sentences.zh: 自幼以孝友聞。

translations.literal: From youth he was known for filial piety and brotherly affection.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood he was known for filial piety and brotherly devotion.

sentences.zh: 至元間，丞相伯顏以師南下，垕是時年未冠，而志強氣銳，率其鄉人見之，論議有合，兵遂不涉其境，鄉人義之。

translations.literal: During the Zhiyuan era Chancellor Bayan marched south with an army; Hou was then not yet capped but strong in will and sharp in spirit; he led his fellow townsmen to see Bayan, their discussion accorded, and the army did not enter their territory; the townspeople honored his righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhiyuan era Chancellor Bayan marched south; Hou was not yet twenty but bold and resolute; he led his townsfolk to meet Bayan, their views aligned, and the army never entered their district—the townspeople honored his courage.

sentences.zh: 伯顏奏授為同知徽州路總管府事，以廉能擢置台憲，累遷至湖南肅政廉訪副使，升浙西廉訪使。

translations.literal: Bayan memorialized to appoint him Associate Administrator of the Huizhou Circuit Intendant's Office; for integrity and ability he was promoted into the surveillance system, rose through posts to Vice Surveillance Commissioner of Hunan, and was advanced to Surveillance Commissioner of Zhexi.
translations.idiomatic: Bayan recommended him as Associate Administrator of Huizhou Circuit; for integrity and ability he entered the surveillance service, rose to Vice Surveillance Commissioner of Hunan, and was promoted to Surveillance Commissioner of Zhexi.

sentences.zh: 所至以黜贓吏、洗冤獄為己任，且嘗上章奏免儒役，及舉行浙西助役法。

translations.literal: Wherever he went he took dismissing corrupt officials and clearing wrongful cases as his charge, and once memorialized to exempt scholars from corvée and to implement the Zhexi mutual-aid corvée law.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he served he made dismissing corrupt officials and clearing wrongful cases his duty; he once memorialized to exempt scholars from corvée and to implement the Zhexi mutual-aid corvée law.

sentences.zh: 年五十卒，賜諡莊簡。

translations.literal: He died at fifty and was granted the posthumous name Zhuangjian.
translations.idiomatic: He died at fifty and was granted the posthumous name Zhuangjian.

sentences.zh: 陳顥，字仲明，其先居盧龍，有名山者，仕金為謀克監軍，太祖得之，以為平陽等路軍民都元帥，子孫徙清州，遂為清州人。

translations.literal: Chen Hao, styled Zhongming, was originally from Lulong; an ancestor named Mingshan served the Jin as a jie'er supervising army, was taken by Taizu, and made commander-in-chief of military and civil affairs of the Pingyang circuit and others; descendants moved to Qingzhou and thus became natives of Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Hao, whose style name was Zhongming, came from Lulong by ancestry; an ancestor named Mingshan had served the Jin as a jie'er army supervisor, was taken into Mongol service by Genghis Khan, and made commander-in-chief of military and civil affairs in Pingyang; his descendants moved to Qingzhou and became Qingzhou natives.

sentences.zh: 顥幼穎悟，日記誦千百言，稍長，遊京師，登翰林承旨王磐、安藏之門。

translations.literal: Hao was quick-witted as a child and could memorize and recite a thousand or more words daily; when somewhat grown he went to the capital and entered the gates of Hanlin Academician Wang Pan and Anzang.
translations.idiomatic: Hao was quick-witted as a boy and could memorize a thousand or more characters a day; when older he went to the capital and studied under Hanlin Academicians Wang Pan and Anzang.

sentences.zh: 磐熟金典章，安藏通諸國語，顥兼習之。

translations.literal: Pan was versed in Jin statutes and regulations; Anzang was fluent in the various national languages; Hao studied both.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Pan knew Jin law and institutions; Anzang was fluent in the languages of many peoples; Hao studied both.

sentences.zh: 安藏乃薦顥入宿衛，尋為仁宗潛邸說書。

translations.literal: Anzang then recommended Hao for palace guard service, and soon he became lecturer at Renzong's hidden residence.
translations.idiomatic: Anzang recommended Hao for palace guard service, and soon he became lecturer at the future Renzong's private residence.

sentences.zh: 於是，仁宗奉母后出居懷慶，顥從行，日開陳以古聖賢居艱貞之道。

translations.literal: Thereupon Renzong escorted the empress dowager out to reside at Huaiqing; Hao accompanied him and daily expounded the way ancient sages and worthies maintained steadfastness in hardship.
translations.idiomatic: When Renzong escorted the empress dowager to Huaiqing, Hao went with him and daily expounded how the ancient sages had borne hardship with steadfast integrity.

sentences.zh: 會成宗崩，仁宗入定內難，以迎武宗，顥皆預謀。

translations.literal: When Chengzong died, Renzong entered the capital to resolve the inner crisis and welcome Wuzong; Hao took part in all the planning.
translations.idiomatic: When Chengzong died, Renzong entered the capital to settle the succession and welcome Wuzong; Hao took part in the planning throughout.

sentences.zh: 及仁宗即位，以推戴舊勳，特拜集賢大學士、榮祿大夫，仍宿衛禁中，政事無不與聞。

translations.literal: When Renzong took the throne, in recognition of his old merit in supporting the enthronement he was specially appointed Grand Academician of the Hall of Gathered Worthies and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, still guarding the inner palace, and was consulted on all government affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Renzong came to the throne, honoring his old service in the enthronement, Hao was specially appointed Grand Academician of the Hall of Gathered Worthies and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness; he continued as palace guard and was consulted on every matter of state.

sentences.zh: 科舉之行，顥贊助之力尤多。

translations.literal: In the restoration of the civil service examinations, Hao's supportive effort was especially great.
translations.idiomatic: In restoring the civil service examinations, Hao's support was especially decisive.

sentences.zh: 顥時伺帝燕閒，輒取聖經所載大經大法有切治體者陳之，每見嘉納。

translations.literal: Hao would wait for the Emperor's leisure moments and present the great principles and laws recorded in the classics that bore on governance; each time he was praised and accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the Emperor was at leisure, Hao would expound the great principles of the classics that bore on governance, and the Emperor always welcomed his counsel.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗坐便殿，群臣入奏事，望見顥，喜曰：「陳仲明在列，所奏必善事矣。

translations.literal: The Emperor once sat in the informal hall as the ministers entered to report affairs; seeing Hao, he said with pleasure, "With Chen Zhongming present, what is reported will surely be good counsel."
translations.idiomatic: Once, as ministers entered the informal hall to report affairs, the Emperor saw Hao and said with pleasure, "With Chen Zhongming here, whatever is reported will surely be sound counsel."

sentences.zh: 」顥以父年老，力請歸養清州，帝特命顥長子孝伯為知州以就養。

translations.literal: " Hao, because his father was old, earnestly requested to return to Qingzhou to support him; the Emperor specially appointed Hao's eldest son Xiaobo as prefect so he could attend to his father's care.
translations.idiomatic: " Hao's father was elderly, and he earnestly asked to return to Qingzhou to care for him; the Emperor specially appointed Hao's eldest son Xiaobo as prefect so the father could be supported nearby.

sentences.zh: 顥固辭，乃以孝伯為州判官。

translations.literal: Hao firmly declined, and Xiaobo was then made vice magistrate of the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Hao firmly declined, and Xiaobo was appointed vice magistrate of the prefecture instead.

sentences.zh: 帝欲用顥為中書平章政事，顥叩首謝曰：「臣無汗馬之功，又乏經濟之略，一旦置之政途，徒速臣咎。

translations.literal: The Emperor wished to use Hao as Director of the Secretariat; Hao bowed his head and declined, saying, "Your servant has no merit of horses sweating in battle, and lacks strategies for ordering the state; to place me suddenly on the path of government would only hasten my blame."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor wished to appoint Hao Director of the Secretariat; Hao kowtowed and declined: "I have no battlefield merit and lack the capacity to govern; to thrust me suddenly into high office would only hasten my downfall."

sentences.zh: 臣願得朝夕左右，獻替可否，庶少裨萬一，亦以全臣愚忠。

translations.literal: Your servant wishes only to remain at Your Majesty's side morning and evening, offering approval or criticism, that I may in some small measure be of use and also preserve my foolish loyalty intact.
translations.idiomatic: I ask only to remain at Your Majesty's side day and night, offering counsel for or against, that I may serve in some small way and preserve my humble loyalty.

sentences.zh: 」帝乃允。

translations.literal: " The Emperor then consented.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor consented.

sentences.zh: 仁宗崩，辭祿家居者十年。

translations.literal: When Renzong died, he resigned his salary and lived at home for ten years.
translations.idiomatic: When Renzong died, he resigned and lived at home for ten years.

sentences.zh: 文宗即位，復起為集賢大學士，上疏勸帝大興文治、增國子學弟子員、蠲儒之徭役，文宗皆嘉納焉。
