translations.literal: When Wenzong took the throne, he was recalled as Grand Academician of the Hall of Gathered Worthies and memorialized urging the Emperor to greatly promote literary governance, increase the quota of students at the Imperial University, and exempt scholars from corvée; Wenzong praised and accepted all of these.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenzong came to the throne, Hao was recalled as Grand Academician of the Hall of Gathered Worthies and memorialized urging a revival of literary governance, more students at the Imperial University, and exemption of scholars from corvée; Wenzong approved them all.

sentences.zh: 顥先後居集賢，署薦士牘累數百，有訐之者，顥曰：「吾寧以謬舉受罰，蔽賢誠所不忍。

translations.literal: During his successive terms at the Hall of Gathered Worthies, Hao signed recommendation documents for scholars numbering in the hundreds; when someone denounced this, Hao said, "I would rather be punished for mistaken recommendation than bear to conceal the worthy."
translations.idiomatic: During his years at the Hall of Gathered Worthies, Hao signed hundreds of recommendations for scholars; when someone accused him of favoritism, he said, "I would rather be punished for a mistaken recommendation than conceal talent."

sentences.zh: 」順帝元統初，顥扈蹕行幸上都，至龍虎台，帝命造膝前，而握其手曰：「卿累朝老臣，更事多矣，凡議政事，宜極言無隱。

translations.literal: " At the beginning of Yuantong under Shundi, Hao accompanied the imperial procession on the journey to Shangdu; at Longhu Terrace the Emperor ordered him brought before him, grasped his hand, and said, "You are an old minister of many reigns and have seen much; in all discussion of government affairs you should speak to the utmost without concealment."
translations.idiomatic: " Early in Yuantong, Hao accompanied Shundi on the journey to Shangdu; at Longhu Terrace the Emperor summoned him, took his hand, and said, "You have served many reigns and seen much; in all matters of state speak your mind without reserve."

sentences.zh: 」顥頓首謝不敏。

translations.literal: " Hao bowed his head and thanked him, pleading his inadequacy.
translations.idiomatic: " Hao kowtowed and thanked him, pleading his inadequacy.

sentences.zh: 顥每集議，其言無不剴切，後至元四年，致政，命食全俸於家。

translations.literal: Whenever Hao joined deliberations, his words were invariably earnest and incisive; in the fourth year of the Later Zhiyuan he retired from office and was ordered to receive his full salary at home.
translations.idiomatic: In every deliberation Hao spoke with earnest incisiveness; in the fourth year of the Later Zhiyuan he retired and was granted his full salary at home.

sentences.zh: 明年卒，年七十六。

translations.literal: The next year he died, aged seventy-six.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he died at the age of seventy-six.

sentences.zh: 至正十四年，贈攄誠秉義佐理功臣、光祿大夫、河南江北等處行中書省平章政事、柱國，追封薊國公，諡文忠。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Zhizheng he was posthumously granted Meritorious Minister Who Expands Sincerity, Upholds Righteousness, and Assists Governance, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Director of the Henan and Jiangbei Branch Secretariat, and Pillar of the State, posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Ji, with the posthumous name Wenzhong.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of Zhizheng he was posthumously honored as Meritorious Minister Who Expands Sincerity, Upholds Righteousness, and Assists Governance, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Director of the Henan and Jiangbei Branch Secretariat, and Pillar of the State, enfeoffed posthumously as Duke of Ji with the posthumous name Wenzhong.

sentences.zh: 顥出入禁闥數十年，樂談人善，而惡聞人過。

translations.literal: Hao entered and left the inner palace gates for decades, delighted to speak of others' virtues and loathing to hear of others' faults.
translations.idiomatic: For decades Hao moved in and out of the inner palace; he loved to speak of others' virtues and hated to hear of their faults.

sentences.zh: 大夫士因其薦拔以至顯列，有終身莫知所自者，是以結知人主，上下無有怨尤。

translations.literal: Great ministers and scholars reached eminent rank through his recommendation; some never knew in their lifetimes from whom they owed their rise—thus he won the sovereign's trust, and above and below there was no resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Many officials rose to prominence through his recommendation, some never knowing who had advanced them; thus he won the sovereign's trust, and court and realm bore him no resentment.

sentences.zh: 歐陽玄為國子祭酒，與顥同考試國子伴讀，每出一卷，顥必拾而觀之，苟得其片言善，即以置選列，為之色喜。

translations.literal: Ouyang Xuan was Chancellor of the Imperial University; he and Hao together examined the university's student readers; whenever a paper was produced, Hao would pick it up and read it, and if he found even a phrase of merit he would place the candidate on the selection list and show delight.
translations.idiomatic: Ouyang Xuan, Chancellor of the Imperial University, examined student readers together with Hao; whenever a paper appeared, Hao would read it, and if he found even one good phrase he would place the candidate on the pass list and rejoice.

sentences.zh: 玄歎曰：「陳公之心，蓋篤於仁而逾於厚者，真可使鄙夫寬、薄夫敦矣。」

translations.literal: Xuan sighed and said, "Master Chen's heart is surely devoted to benevolence and surpasses even generosity—it can truly make the mean broad and the shallow earnest."
translations.idiomatic: Ouyang sighed and said, "Master Chen's heart is steeped in benevolence beyond ordinary generosity—it could truly broaden the petty and deepen the shallow."

sentences.zh: 次子敬伯，至正中仕為中書參知政事，歷左丞、右丞，二十七年，拜中書平章政事。

translations.literal: His second son Jingbo, during the Zhizheng era served as Vice Director of the Secretariat, passed through Left and Right Chancellor, and in the twenty-seventh year was appointed Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His second son Jingbo served in the Zhizheng era as Vice Director of the Secretariat, rose through Left and Right Chancellor, and in the twenty-seventh year was appointed Director of the Secretariat.
